Best digital legacy vaults (2026)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026 · Independent: sponsors can't buy a verdict · How we rate

For most people, the best digital legacy setup is a password manager with emergency access (Bitwarden or Keeper) plus a planning vault for documents and wishes (Everplans, Prisidio or GoodTrust). The free Google and Apple legacy settings belong on top of either.

Key facts

  • #1 Everplans: Organised planners who want a guided inventory of accounts, wishes and documents.
  • #2 Prisidio: US households who want one shared vault for documents, valuables and stories.
  • #3 GoodTrust: US families who want estate documents and digital-account planning in one place.
  • #4 Bitwarden: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.
  • #5 Keeper: People who want emergency access alongside business-grade security features.
  • #6 Trustworthy: Families who want one organised, shareable place for important documents.
  • #7 MyWishes: People who want a free way to record digital and end-of-life wishes.
  • #8 SecureSafe: Existing SecureSafe Classic users who already set up data inheritance.
  • #9 Life Ledger: Families handling a UK estate who want to notify many companies at once.
  • #10 Settld: Families handling a UK estate after a death.

Quick picks

  • Best overall: Everplans (Good) · Free + paid
  • Runner-up: Prisidio (Good) · Paid
  • Also good: GoodTrust (Good) · Paid

Which should you choose?

1. Everplans Official site ↗

Best for: Organised planners who want a guided inventory of accounts, wishes and documents.

A well-structured digital vault for life admin and end-of-life plans that you can securely share with people you trust.

Pricing: Free base app; Everplans Premium is paid. Check current pricing.

2. Prisidio Official site ↗

Best for: US households who want one shared vault for documents, valuables and stories.

A family 'life readiness' vault with a Co-Owner and a Keyholder who can get the vault after a verified death, with identity checks via CLEAR.

Pricing: Check current pricing.

3. GoodTrust Official site ↗

Best for: US families who want estate documents and digital-account planning in one place.

An all-in-one US estate planning platform: will, trust and directives (valid in all 50 states) plus a Digital Vault for your digital life.

Pricing: Estate+ plan advertised at $149 (US). Check current pricing.

4. Bitwarden Official site ↗

Best for: Budget-conscious people who want a proper, tested emergency-access workflow.

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.

Pricing: Free plan available; Emergency Access requires Premium or a paid Families/Teams/Enterprise plan. Check current pricing.

5. Keeper Official site ↗

Best for: People who want emergency access alongside business-grade security features.

A solid choice with built-in Emergency Access: name trusted contacts who can request your vault after a wait period.

Pricing: Paid plans with a free trial. Check current pricing.

6. Trustworthy Official site ↗

Best for: Families who want one organised, shareable place for important documents.

A family document organiser with an encrypted vault and legacy access options. It organises information; it doesn't say it writes wills.

Pricing: Free plan; Silver $10, Gold $20, Platinum $40 a month, paid annually. Check current pricing.

7. MyWishes Official site ↗

Best for: People who want a free way to record digital and end-of-life wishes.

A free UK-based platform to write a will, a 'Digital & Social Media Will', funeral wishes and an advance care plan, then download, print and share them.

Pricing: Free.

8. SecureSafe Official site ↗

Best for: Existing SecureSafe Classic users who already set up data inheritance.

A Swiss-hosted vault whose data inheritance (activator code plus a blocking period) is only in SecureSafe Classic; SecureSafe says the new app doesn't have it.

Pricing: Check official pricing.

9. Life Ledger Official site ↗

Best for: Families handling a UK estate who want to notify many companies at once.

A free UK death notification service: notify over 1,000 UK companies of a death from one place and track progress online.

Pricing: Free, with unlimited notifications.

10. Settld Official site ↗

Best for: Families handling a UK estate after a death.

A free UK bereavement admin service that reports a death to multiple companies in one go and tracks updates in one secure space.

Pricing: Free to use.

Frequently asked questions

What are the best digital legacy vaults?

For most people, the best digital legacy setup is a password manager with emergency access (Bitwarden or Keeper) plus a planning vault for documents and wishes (Everplans, Prisidio or GoodTrust). The free Google and Apple legacy settings belong on top of either.

Is Everplans a good choice?

A well-structured digital vault for life admin and end-of-life plans that you can securely share with people you trust.

Is Prisidio a good choice?

A family 'life readiness' vault with a Co-Owner and a Keyholder who can get the vault after a verified death, with identity checks via CLEAR.

Is GoodTrust a good choice?

An all-in-one US estate planning platform: will, trust and directives (valid in all 50 states) plus a Digital Vault for your digital life.

Is Bitwarden a good choice?

The best-value password manager with real emergency access: trusted contacts can request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set.
